title: 新疆巡回医疗实现能力薄弱县乡村全覆盖
content: 当前位置： 首页 / 机构概况 / 机构设置 / 新闻宣传 / 新闻宣传 新疆巡回医疗实现能力薄弱县乡村全覆盖 2026年11月05日 11时47分 【字体：大 中 小】 【打印本文】 浏览量：次 石榴云/新疆日报讯（记者 苏璐萍报道）11月4日，记者从自治区人民政府新闻办公室召开的“推进医疗卫生强基工程 守护各族群众生命健康”——“完整准确全面贯彻新时代党的治疆方略”系列主题新闻发布会（第5场）获悉，新疆已全面建立自治区、地、县、乡、村五级巡回医疗制度，2026年组建14支自治区级和71支地（州、市）级巡回医疗队，派出医疗队员711人，县级医院和乡镇卫生院向乡、村两级巡诊1.16万次，服务群众300多万人次，能力薄弱县乡村实现全覆盖。 11月4日，自治区人民政府新闻办公室召开“推进医疗卫生强基工程 守护各族群众生命健康”——“完整准确全面贯彻新时代党的治疆方略”系列主题新闻发布会（第5场）。图为发布会现场。石榴云/新疆日报记者 周鹏摄 “流动医院”成为常态。自治区级医院巡回医疗覆盖14个地（州、市）医疗服务能力薄弱县和边远乡镇，地（州、市）级医院巡回医疗覆盖辖区内所有县（市、区）及能力薄弱乡镇、村。自治区级、地（州、市）级医院每年下沉2至3次，县级巡回医疗每季度至少1次，乡镇卫生院对村卫生室巡诊每月至少2次。还有9支国家医疗队到全区9个地州24个县（市、区），根据当地就医需求选派专家，群众在家门口就能看上“专家号”。 边境县有了“巡诊车+移动手术室”。新疆在边境县（市）推行“巡诊车+移动手术室”和“巡诊车+移动诊疗设备”，把检查、小手术送到牧民身边。完善县区医疗急救体系，改善装备条件，畅通急救服务绿色通道，到2030年实现每个县区组建并强化1支背囊化医疗应急小分队，完善血液供需联动保障机制，增设采血点。 3月18日，阿克苏市启动2026年巡回医疗服务活动。医务人员深入乡村，开展义诊咨询、慢性病随访等一站式便民服务（资料图）。赵鑫 摄 远程医疗让“基层检查、上级诊断”成为可能。全区已建成互联网医院62家，以省级2个远程会诊中心为依托开展远程会诊1.7万例。伊犁哈萨克自治州建成覆盖州、县、乡、村四级医疗信息平台，实现“基层检查、上级诊断”；吉木萨尔县为村医配备智慧助诊包，打造“行走的医院”，全县基层就诊率稳定在66%以上。 自治区卫生健康委党组成员，自治区中医药管理局党组书记、局长刘波表示，将持续优化巡回医疗的频次和覆盖面，推动常态化巡回医疗与远程诊疗、“固定+流动”服务模式更好衔接，让偏远农牧区群众能就近看得上病、看得好病。 相关附件>> 扫一扫在手机打开当前页

title: 新疆基层中医馆覆盖率超99% 基本实现15分钟中医药服务圈
content: 当前位置： 首页 / 机构概况 / 机构设置 / 新闻宣传 / 新闻宣传 新疆基层中医馆覆盖率超99% 基本实现15分钟中医药服务圈 2026年11月05日 11时42分 【字体：大 中 小】 【打印本文】 浏览量：次 石榴云/新疆日报讯（记者 苏璐萍报道）11月4日，记者从自治区人民政府新闻办公室召开的“推进医疗卫生强基工程 守护各族群众生命健康”——“完整准确全面贯彻新时代党的治疆方略”系列主题新闻发布会（第5场）获悉，目前，新疆14个地州市政府办公立中医医院实现全覆盖，基层中医馆设置率超过99%，基本实现15分钟中医药服务圈。 11月4日，自治区卫生健康委党组成员，自治区中医药管理局党组书记、局长刘波就基层中医药服务答记者问。刘凯 摄 近年来，新疆持续完善中医药服务网络、提升专科能力、加强重点人群健康管理和中西医协同，服务网络覆盖城乡。全区已建成1353所中医医疗机构，县办中医医疗机构覆盖率达86.7%，综合医院中医科设置率达100%。群众有个头疼脑热、颈肩腰腿痛，在乡镇卫生院、社区卫生服务中心就能找到中医馆。 专科能力向基层延伸。建设一批国家中医优势专科、自治区中医优势专科和自治区中医优势专科联盟，推动形成专科集群；重点加强老年病科、儿科、神经病科、康复科等科室建设，支持60家县级中医医院开展“两专科一中心”项目建设，基层中医药服务的可及性、便捷性持续提高。 重点人群健康管理加强。各县（市、区）老年人、儿童中医药健康管理率分别达81.87%、88.18%。新疆首次申请公益基金，支持开展中小学生肥胖、近视、龋齿及重点人群布病中西医结合干预防治；配合教育部门落实中小学生脊柱筛查，印发脊柱侧弯中医药综合防控技术方案。 中西医协同和人才培养同步推进。指导国家中西医协同“旗舰”医院建设，支持中西医结合“旗舰”科室建设，建成41个全国基层名老中医药专家传承工作室；面向县级医疗机构西医医师开展系统化“西学中”专项培训，组织全疆乡镇卫生院、社区卫生服务中心1700多名中医馆在岗人才开展专项能力培训，让群众在基层就能获得中医药服务。 自治区卫生健康委党组成员，自治区中医药管理局党组书记、局长刘波表示，将加强县级综合医院中医科建设，推动乡镇卫生院、社区卫生服务中心中医馆提质增效，扩大中医药人才培养供给规模，提升边境县市中医药服务能力，让更多群众就近享受中医药服务。 相关附件>> 扫一扫在手机打开当前页

title: HHS Awards More Than $3 Million to Strengthen Nutrition Services for Older Adults
content: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE November 17, 2026 Contact: HHS Press Office 202-690-6343 Submit a Request for Comment HHS Awards More Than $3 Million to Strengthen Nutrition Services for Older Adults WASHINGTON, D.C.—NOVEMBER 17, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Administration for Community Living (ACL), today announced a cooperative agreement totaling more than $3 million to USAging for the National Resource Center on Nutrition and Aging (NRCNA). The three-year award will strengthen Senior Nutrition Programs, funded by the Older Americans Act, by providing national leadership, training, technical assistance, data infrastructure, and resources that help communities improve nutrition services for older adults.This investment supports the Trump Administration’s Make America Healthy Again agenda by strengthening nutrition services that help prevent disease, reduce isolation, and advance whole-person health.“Good nutrition is one of our most powerful tools for preventing chronic disease and helping Americans stay healthy and independent as they age,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “The Trump Administration is expanding access to real, nutritious food and practical nutrition support for older adults across the country. This investment will strengthen the local programs that help older Americans protect their health and live with dignity.”Good nutrition is essential to healthy aging, helping older adults maintain their health, independence, and quality of life. Yet an estimated 10 million older adults face hunger each year, and many others struggle to access nutritious food and supportive services. Senior Nutrition Programs serve nearly 1 million meals a day to older adults across the United States through roughly 5,000 local providers. Further, a nutrition intervention is more than a meal: It provides a mix of food, guidance, and connection that supports both physical health and well-being.Helping More Adults Stay Nourished and ConnectedThe resource center’s goal is to increase participation in nutrition, socialization, and health promotion activities by 15 percent by 2029. To get there, it will work with Innovations in Nutrition grantees, State Units on Aging and Area Agencies on Aging, 70 Title VI Native American aging programs, and more than 5,000 local nutrition providers across the country.The center also will support efforts to connect at least half of older adult participants to nutrition or health-promotion services and help more than 60 percent maintain or improve their nutrition risk scores.“For many older adults, a nutrition intervention is also a connection to community, a wellness check, and a lifeline to other supports,” said Mary Lazare, ACL Principal Deputy Administrator. “The National Resource Center on Nutrition and Aging will help communities strengthen and expand these services so more older adults can access the nutritious food, trusted support, and community connections they need to stay healthy and independent.”Supporting the Local Programs That Help Older Adults ThriveStrong local programs are essential to meeting the needs of a growing older population. The NRCNA will support the local organizations that deliver Senior Nutrition Programs, helping them reach more older adults and improve the quality of the meals, education, and connection they offer. The center will also identify and share successful approaches from communities across the country, publish accessible resources, and help aging network partners learn from one another to advance whole-person health for older adults.USAging is the national association representing and supporting the network of Area Agencies on Aging and advocating for the Title VI Native American Aging Programs. ### Note: All HHS press releases, fact sheets and other news materials are available in our Press Room.Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.Last revised: November 17, 2026

title: HHS Announces 41 States Have Ended the ‘Orphan Tax,’ Urges Remaining 9 to Stop Diverting Survivor Benefits from Foster Children
content: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE November 16, 2026 Contact: HHS Press Office 202-690-6343 Submit a Request for Comment HHS Announces 41 States Have Ended the ‘Orphan Tax,’ Urges Remaining 9 to Stop Diverting Survivor Benefits from Foster Children WASHINGTON, D.C.—NOVEMBER 16, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) through the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) today renewed its call for states to end the “orphan tax” by sending updated letters to the nine governors whose states continue to divert Social Security survivor benefits from foster youth. The letters inform governors of a new ACF technical assistance center available to provide support to states as they choose to end the orphan tax.Since ACF’s initial outreach in December 2025 to 39 governors, 30 states have taken decisive action to end or substantially reform this practice: Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Michigan, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, North Dakota, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Washington, West Virginia, and Wyoming.These states join the 11 states and the District of Columbia that previously ended the orphan tax prior to December 2025: Arizona, California, Colorado, Kansas, Massachusetts, Missouri, Nevada, New Mexico, Ohio, Oregon, Virginia.“Every child deserves the financial security their parents worked hard to provide,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “These benefits are often the last lifeline a parent can leave behind for their child. The Trump Administration will fight to ensure no state can seize these funds through this unconscionable practice.”“We have seen tremendous bipartisan leadership from governors and state legislatures, proving that preserving these benefits can be done,” said Assistant Secretary Alex J. Adams. “These children have already lost their parents — diverting their survivor benefits just adds unnecessary hardship to unimaginable grief. We are calling on every remaining state to stop balancing budgets on the backs of orphans.”With 41 states (82%) ending or substantially reforming the practice, there are just nine states (18%) remaining that are diverting survivor benefits from orphans: Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Maryland, Minnesota, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Wisconsin.Every governor has the authority to end this practice today without the need for legislative action. Multiple states, including Nebraska, Louisiana, Indiana, and Oklahoma have ended the orphan tax through an executive order.In addition to the governors’ letter, ACF sent a corresponding letter to the National Association of State Budget Officers (NASBO) encouraging increased coordination and communication between child welfare agencies and state budget officers to solve this issue.Through the newly announced technical assistance center, ACF is available to work with state budget offices to help address perceived funding gaps that may arise when survivor benefits are no longer diverted to offset state funding obligations. While the national estimate of budget impact is that diverting orphans’ survivor benefits nets to just 0.22% of a state’s child welfare budget, there may be potential offsets available through Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funding and Title IV-E adoption savings.The new letters come just one year after President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump signed the Fostering the Future for American Children and Families Executive Order, spurring action across the federal government to do more to protect foster children. Thanks to the First Lady’s leadership, states can now use Fostering the Future Accounts to preserve survivor benefits for foster youth. Already, more than half the states across the nation have chosen to create Fostering the Future Accounts for foster children, providing foster children with a strong financial foundation as they enter adulthood. ### Note: All HHS press releases, fact sheets and other news materials are available in our Press Room.Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.Last revised: November 16, 2026

title: 新疆新闻联播 情满天山 援疆印记丨苏州（张家港）医疗援疆筑牢巩留县域健康防线
content: 当前位置： 首页 / 机构概况 / 机构设置 / 新闻宣传 / 新闻宣传 新疆新闻联播 情满天山 援疆印记丨苏州（张家港）医疗援疆筑牢巩留县域健康防线 2026年11月13日 18时55分 【字体：大 中 小】 【打印本文】 浏览量：次 新疆广播电视台/丝路视听讯（新疆台伊犁台肖开提尹芝盛巩留台阿力马斯）江苏省苏州（张家港）援疆医疗工作组聚焦巩留县基层医疗短板，坚持诊疗帮扶与人才培育同步推进，推动优质医疗资源落地基层。 立冬节气后，寒热交替的气温让巩留县东买里镇公尚村村民马军受了凉，这两天正在巩留县总医院东买里镇分院接受治疗。 巩留县东买里镇公尚村村民马军：换季感冒，就来我们这附近的卫生院做一个中西医的治疗，刚才在做中医的刮痧和拔火罐，也是比较方便的见效也快。 依托援疆资源，巩留县东买里镇分院持续补强专科能力，在中医诊疗之外，新增中医妇科、骨伤科。援疆专家常态化下沉，开展儿童生长发育、行为语言发育筛查，建立筛查、评估、康复、随访闭环管理机制。 江苏省苏州（张家港）柔性援疆干部人才蔡婧晔：下沉基层，不仅为孩子开展筛查、个性化的指导及相关的诊疗，也会手把手地带教我们本地的医护人员，把成熟的儿童发育评估以及一些干预的方法留在基层。 巩留县总医院东买里镇分院党支部书记王甜：这次柔性援疆妇幼儿童康复专家下沉坐诊，补齐了我们的专科短板。我们会不断做强特色专科，让老百姓在家门口享受到更全面的医疗服务。 今年以来，14名张家港援疆医疗人才累计开展义诊带教38场次，服务群众3200多人次。借力援疆帮扶资源，巩留县诊疗条件不断完善，多项医疗技术空白得以填补。 江苏省苏州（张家港）医疗援疆专家领队巩留县总医院人民医院院区副院长孙晓峰：今年以来张家港援疆医疗人才在巩留落地推广新技术15项，填补本地医疗技术空白12项，成功开展各类手术516台，有效降低了县域危重患者外转率。通过师带徒、院包科、进修培养等方式带教本土医师12名。 相关附件>> 扫一扫在手机打开当前页
